title: The characterization of graphs with tree reconfiguration graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote its reconfiguration graph. Here, $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is the graph whose vertices represent minimal domination sets of $G$, with adjacency given by the reconfiguration relation defined in the paper. Let $\overline{K_n}$ be the edgeless graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_{1,m}$ be the star with $m$ leaves, and let $\cup$ denote disjoint union.

**Tree reconfiguration graph conjecture.** $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is a tree if and only if

$$
G \cong \overline{K_n} \cup K_{1,m}
$$

for some non-negative integers $m$ and $n$.

The conjecture seeks a complete characterization of graphs whose minimal-domination-set reconfiguration graph is a tree. The paper establishes several related connectivity and characterization results, but the stated equivalence is presented as a conjecture.
source_name: Iain Beaton, “Reconfiguration graphs for minimal domination sets”, arXiv:2411.02300 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).
